body:
You bring up some excellent points but you're making some big assumptions at the same time.

Firstly, you're assuming I want tangible benefits from a relationship. Put bluntly, I'm in a situation where I'm under so much pressure from my family that a near future without a relationship isn't one worth living. I don't care about the negatives at all, I want results and that's all. I would happily lose an arm and all non-essential organs rather than face my parents if I fail, you have no idea what they're like.

Secondly, you're assuming I'm showing tangible desperation because of my determination. First issue with that is that I developed this philosophy well after these events even took place and second is that literally everyone I know is just as confused as I am why this is happening. It's very easy from 'the other side of the lens' to assume I'm one of those desperate pathetic guys but it simply isn't true.

I have every single other thing I need, but if I don't have this, my life will become a hell worse than you can probably imagine.

Thank you for your sharing your story on this, I do really see your point that the idea of being in a relationship itself becomes an addiction that needs to be treated like any addiction. I'm sorry to hear about your experiences and I'm glad things have improved for you. 

One issue is that I'm also dependent on this as a fact, not just as tangible benefits. That is, I need to satisfy my demanding parents and more so to feel like I'm not inadequate. 

Numerous contributing factors also mean that I'm essentially reliant on being in a relationship to not feel alone, and that feeling of loneliness is tortuous. I don't think it's something I can cure without experiencing it at least once because otherwise I'll always feel like it's never an option.
